name: toolaby

tools.name: toolaby_whoami
tools.description: The developer signed in to Toolaby (Test) and their workspaces, each with its role and the address its buyers use.

tools.name: toolaby_list_tools
tools.description: Every tool in the developer's workspaces on Toolaby (Test), with the id the other tools take.

tools.name: toolaby_get_tool
tools.description: One tool on Toolaby (Test). Read it before changing it. freePlan says what the Free plan holds (freePlan.holds, in a sentence); features are the keys gate({ feature }) takes; plans say what each unlocks (plans[].features), with the id openPaymentPage(id) and data-toolaby-plan take; toolKey is what toolaby.config.js must hold (else `npx -y toolaby@latest upgrade <id>`); extension.checkedInAt says whether a copy has checked in; sale says whether anything can be bought, as the dashboard says it (label, and fix: stripe or price); pages.buyer is the checkout page, pages.webScript the <script src> of toolaby-web.js for a website, pages.api the REST API's base on this side.

tool.description: The tool id, as toolaby_list_tools gives it (like "acme--word-counter"); the short one ("word-counter") works when it names one tool.

tools.name: toolaby_list_customers
tools.description: The tool's customers on Toolaby (Test): everyone who holds or held it, with how (licence, subscription, trial, grant) and whether they are entitled now. `query` filters by an address or a name, in part.

tool.description: The tool id, as toolaby_list_tools gives it (like "acme--word-counter"); the short one ("word-counter") works when it names one tool.

query.description: Optional: part of an address or a name.

tools.name: toolaby_get_customer
tools.description: One buyer of the tool on Toolaby (Test): whether they hold it now and how (entitledVia, plan, features), their licences, subscriptions (status, renews, endsAt, trialEnd) and grants, each with the id refund, cancel and revoke take, and how many devices they use. Answers 404 when the address holds nothing of the tool.

tool.description: The tool id, as toolaby_list_tools gives it (like "acme--word-counter"); the short one ("word-counter") works when it names one tool.

tools.name: toolaby_search_docs
tools.description: Searches Toolaby's docs. Call this before writing Toolaby code or answering how something works, even when you think you know: it gives the pages and sections that match, with the page name toolaby_docs reads.

tools.name: toolaby_docs
tools.description: Toolaby's docs as Markdown. Without a page: the index, every page with what it covers. With a page (like "gating", "pricing", "agents", "reference/client"): that page.

tools.name: toolaby_check
tools.description: Checks an extension folder's Toolaby wiring and answers findings with stable codes ({ code, level, message, file, line, fix, docs }); ok is false when any is an error. Run it before saying the work is done. `built`: a build folder (like ".output/chrome-mv3" or "dist") to check as the build. `browser`: also load the extension in Chromium and ask its background (downloads Playwright and Chromium once, about 180 MB). `as`: with browser, enter the test licence `toolaby_test_unlock` made for this plan and confirm its features unlock.

folder.description: The extension's folder, absolute or relative to where the server started. Default: there.

built.description: Optional: a build folder to check as the build.

as.description: A plan id, as toolaby_get_tool lists them (the first plan is "default").

tools.name: toolaby_stripe_status
tools.description: Whether a workspace sells through Stripe yet on Test, and where a person connects it. Connecting is Stripe's own onboarding (identity, bank, terms): only a person can do it, in a browser. On Test every workspace has a test account already.

workspace.description: The workspace slug, when you have more than one (toolaby_whoami lists them).

tools.name: toolaby_sign_in
tools.description: Signs the command line and this server in to Toolaby (Test). Answers a link and a code for the person to approve in their browser — show them both — and keeps waiting in the background: once they approve, every other tool works. Already signed in: says who.

tools.name: toolaby_create_tool
tools.description: A new tool on Toolaby (Test): one more thing the workspace sells. Its Free plan holds everything until access is set. Then wire an extension to it: `npx -y toolaby@latest wire <id>` in an existing extension's folder, `npx -y toolaby@latest create <id>` for a new one.

id.description: Optional: the id within the workspace. Default: from the name.

tagline.description: Optional: one line under the name on the checkout page.

workspace.description: The workspace slug, when you have more than one (toolaby_whoami lists them).

tools.name: toolaby_update_tool
tools.description: The tool's name, its line, its description, or its Chrome Web Store listing (the store link or the 32-letter id), on Test. Only what is sent changes. The store listing makes the store's copy one the tool key opens for: set it once the item exists.

tool.description: The tool id, as toolaby_list_tools gives it (like "acme--word-counter"); the short one ("word-counter") works when it names one tool.

annotations.title: Change a tool's words or store listing

tools.name: toolaby_set_access
tools.description: What a buyer gets before paying, on Test: "open" (the tool's use, unlimited), "free_uses" (a number of uses per device, or per account with signInRequired, counted by gate() without a feature: for good, or each day, week or month with freeUsesPer, counted by Toolaby in UTC), or "paid" (nothing before a plan). Whichever it is, a feature a plan sells (not marked free) is refused until bought. signInRequired asks for an account first. Takes effect on every device at its next check, with no release — so moving from "free_uses" to "open" would let copies already installed that gate with a bare gate() run everything free until they update: while copies are installed it is refused. Keep "free_uses": opening it is the person's step, once the build that gates by feature is live on the store — tell them, with the command the refusal names. The answer says when the tool key changed: then `npx -y toolaby@latest upgrade <id>`.

tool.description: The tool id, as toolaby_list_tools gives it (like "acme--word-counter"); the short one ("word-counter") works when it names one tool.

freeUses.description: With "free_uses": how many per device, or per account with signInRequired (at most 200 a day).

freeUsesPer.description: With "free_uses": how often they start again — "ever" (never, the default), or each UTC day, week (from Monday) or month. A daily allowance is this, not code.

annotations.title: Set what the Free plan holds

tools.name: toolaby_set_features
tools.description: The tool's whole feature list — send the features it keeps too: one left out is archived, never deleted (off the checkout, still held by the plans that held it, still answered for code that asks; sent again, it is listed again) — and which plans unlock which. Add the plans first (toolaby_add_plan), then this. A feature's key is what the extension passes to gate({ feature }) and has(). A feature marked free is on the Free plan too; one not free that no plan unlocks is refused to everyone. Naming one plan of a tier (plans that share a name, like "Pro" monthly and yearly) sets the whole tier. The answer lists what each plan unlocks now.

tool.description: The tool id, as toolaby_list_tools gives it (like "acme--word-counter"); the short one ("word-counter") works when it names one tool.

name.description: What buyers see, like "Export to CSV".

blurb.description: Optional: one sentence the paywall shows.

plans.description: For each plan id, the feature keys it unlocks.

annotations.title: Set features, and the plans that unlock them

tools.name: toolaby_add_plan
tools.description: A plan buyers can buy: a Price on the workspace's Stripe account (on Test, its test account). "one_time" is a lifetime licence (by default on the tool's devices, sold per seat); "subscription" bills monthly or yearly (any devices, one person). Answers the plan's id (the first is "default") — what openPaymentPage(id) and data-toolaby-plan take — then say what it unlocks with toolaby_set_features. Two plans with one name are one tier. The answer says when the tool key changed: then `npx -y toolaby@latest upgrade <id>`.

tool.description: The tool id, as toolaby_list_tools gives it (like "acme--word-counter"); the short one ("word-counter") works when it names one tool.

amount.description: In the currency's main unit, like 9.99.

name.description: Optional: the plan's name, its tier, like "Pro". Buyers read it before the billing ("Pro · Monthly"), so never the billing word itself.

devices.description: Optional: devices one buyer may use at once.

perSeat.description: Optional: sold per seat, to teams. Default: yes for one_time, no for a subscription.

tools.name: toolaby_update_plan
tools.description: A plan's name (its tier), free trial, devices or per seat. Only what is sent changes. The price never changes: a new price is a new plan (toolaby_add_plan), and the old one is retired (toolaby_retire_plan).

tool.description: The tool id, as toolaby_list_tools gives it (like "acme--word-counter"); the short one ("word-counter") works when it names one tool.

plan.description: A plan id, as toolaby_get_tool lists them (the first plan is "default").

tools.name: toolaby_retire_plan
tools.description: Takes a plan off sale: its Stripe price is archived and nobody can buy it any more. Everyone who bought it keeps what they bought.

tool.description: The tool id, as toolaby_list_tools gives it (like "acme--word-counter"); the short one ("word-counter") works when it names one tool.

plan.description: A plan id, as toolaby_get_tool lists them (the first plan is "default").

tools.name: toolaby_grant
tools.description: Access to the tool's paid features without paying, for an address: a friend, a beta tester, a refund made good. It applies once that person signs in to the extension with that address (a sign-in link by email). For a store reviewer, who cannot receive a sign-in link, make a coupon instead (toolaby_create_coupon). For a number of days, or until revoked; answers the grant id toolaby_revoke_grant takes. On Hobby a workspace holds 100 grants and other passes live at once.

tool.description: The tool id, as toolaby_list_tools gives it (like "acme--word-counter"); the short one ("word-counter") works when it names one tool.

days.description: Optional: how long. Default: until revoked.

tools.name: toolaby_revoke_grant
tools.description: Takes back access given without paying: the person loses it at their next check. The id comes from toolaby_grant's answer or toolaby_get_customer.

tool.description: The tool id, as toolaby_list_tools gives it (like "acme--word-counter"); the short one ("word-counter") works when it names one tool.

tools.name: toolaby_create_coupon
tools.description: A coupon code buyers type on the checkout page, on the workspace's Stripe account (Test). The Chrome Web Store reviewer's way in: percentOff 100, maxRedemptions 1, a few days, and the code in the item's test instructions. percentOff or amountOff (with currency); once, for some months ("repeating" + months), or for ever on a subscription.

tool.description: The tool id, as toolaby_list_tools gives it (like "acme--word-counter"); the short one ("word-counter") works when it names one tool.

tools.name: toolaby_refund
tools.description: Refunds a buyer's lifetime licence in full on their card and revokes it at once; Stripe keeps its fee and Toolaby keeps its own. By the buyer's address (when they have one paid licence) or a licence id from toolaby_get_customer. A subscription's payment is refunded in the Stripe Dashboard; end the subscription with toolaby_cancel_subscription.

tool.description: The tool id, as toolaby_list_tools gives it (like "acme--word-counter"); the short one ("word-counter") works when it names one tool.

licence.description: Optional: the licence id, when they have several.

tools.name: toolaby_cancel_subscription
tools.description: Ends a buyer's subscription: at the end of the period they paid for (they keep access until then), or now. Nothing is refunded. By the buyer's address (when they have one running) or a subscription id from toolaby_get_customer.

tool.description: The tool id, as toolaby_list_tools gives it (like "acme--word-counter"); the short one ("word-counter") works when it names one tool.

now.description: End it now, not at the period's end.

tools.name: toolaby_test_unlock
tools.description: Test only. A licence for one of the tool's plans, for the developer's own +toolaby-test address, with no payment: then toolaby_check with browser and as: <plan> enters it in the loaded extension and confirms the plan's features unlock. Proves the paid path with no person and no card. Each call makes a new one (a pass on Hobby).

tool.description: The tool id, as toolaby_list_tools gives it (like "acme--word-counter"); the short one ("word-counter") works when it names one tool.

plan.description: A plan id, as toolaby_get_tool lists them (the first plan is "default").

tools.name: toolaby_copy_to_live
tools.description: Copies a tool from Test to Live — its Free plan, features, plans (as prices on the Live Stripe account), extension identity and versions — and answers the Live tool key. Done again later, it updates what changed. Needs the command line signed in on both sides (`npx -y toolaby@latest login` and `login --live`) as the same person, and Stripe taking payments on Live for the plans: copied before, the plans stay on Test until it is copied again. The answer's dashboard is the tool's page on Live, which lists what is left. Then `npx -y toolaby@latest upgrade <id> --live` writes the Live key into the extension before the store build.

tool.description: The tool id, as toolaby_list_tools gives it (like "acme--word-counter"); the short one ("word-counter") works when it names one tool.

tools.name: toolaby_create_api_key
tools.description: A secret API key for the developer's own server (Toolaby's REST API, Test), written into an env file as TOOLABY_API_KEY, with the API's base for this side as TOOLABY_API_URL, and never shown: the answer says where it went, not what it is. The file is created if missing; a TOOLABY_API_KEY line already there is replaced. Make sure the file is in .gitignore.

envFile.description: The env file, like ".env" (relative to where the server started) or an absolute path.

name.description: Optional: what the key is for, like "Server".

workspace.description: The workspace slug, when you have more than one (toolaby_whoami lists them).

tools.name: toolaby_list_webhook_events
tools.description: The events Toolaby sends a registered endpoint — purchases, subscriptions started and cancelled, refunds, disputes — each with a description and an example of what it carries, for the handler that reads them.

tools.name: toolaby_list_webhooks
tools.description: The endpoints registered on Test: id, address, the events each listens for, and whether it is paused.

workspace.description: The workspace slug, when you have more than one (toolaby_whoami lists them).

tools.name: toolaby_add_webhook
tools.description: Registers the developer's server to receive Toolaby's events on Test, and writes its signing secret into an env file as TOOLABY_WEBHOOK_SECRET, never shown. A server that mirrors buyers gets no event until its endpoint is registered: on Test, this is yours to do as part of the job, not a step to leave to the person; toolaby_remove_webhook undoes it. The url is the server's public address and the handler's path (a tunnel's while developing, like https://…trycloudflare.com/webhooks/toolaby).

url.description: The public https address of the handler.

envFile.description: The env file the server reads, like ".env", for TOOLABY_WEBHOOK_SECRET.

events.description: Optional: only these events (toolaby_list_webhook_events); all of them when left out.

workspace.description: The workspace slug, when you have more than one (toolaby_whoami lists them).

tools.name: toolaby_send_test_event
tools.description: Sends an event's example to every endpoint registered on Test that listens for it, as a real, signed delivery: the way to see a handler answer 2xx. 100 a day per workspace.

workspace.description: The workspace slug, when you have more than one (toolaby_whoami lists them).

tools.name: toolaby_remove_webhook
tools.description: Removes an endpoint: deliveries to it stop at once.

id.description: The endpoint id, as toolaby_list_webhooks gives it.

workspace.description: The workspace slug, when you have more than one (toolaby_whoami lists them).

instructions:
Toolaby (Test): paid plans, licences, subscriptions and the paywall for Chrome extensions, on the developer's own Stripe. Search the docs first (toolaby_search_docs). Read a tool (toolaby_get_tool) before changing it; add plans, then features. Gate paid code with toolaby.gate({ feature }). Verify with toolaby_check, then toolaby_test_unlock + toolaby_check { browser, as }. Not signed in: toolaby_sign_in.

The project you are working in is usually the extension: when it has no toolaby.config.js, wire it yourself with the shell (npx -y toolaby@latest wire <id>; upgrade <id> after a key change) — it is not a step for the person — then gate its work in code as TOOLABY.md says. Every tool here has the same command (npx -y toolaby@latest <words> --json). This is Test: nothing here charges anyone. Never report a step a person must do (approve sign-in, connect Stripe on Live, upload to the store, a real purchase) as done.
